questions: Can the same index j be set to 1 multiple times through different operations, or is setting it once sufficient?
Is there any constraint on how many times each type of operation (Operation 0, 1, 2) can be used?
Are the indices L_i and R_i inclusive bounds for the range of elements affected by Operations 1 and 2?
Does "Do nothing" in Operation 0 mean that the sequence remains unchanged, including positions outside [L_i, R_i]?
What happens if both Operation 1 and Operation 2 could potentially set the same element to 1 during different operations?
Must every position from 1 to N be set to 1 at least once, or is it sufficient for all to end up as 1 regardless of when they were set?
In the output format, should K represent the total number of operations performed, or is it related to the cost?
If multiple solutions exist with the same minimal cost, which specific solution should be printed?
answers: Setting it once is sufficient; additional sets have no effect on the goal.
No constraint on the number of times each operation can be used.
Yes. Both L_i and R_i are inclusive bounds defining the affected range.
Yes. Operation 0 has no effect on any positions in the sequence.
Both can set the same element to 1; the effect is simply that the element becomes 1.
Yes. Every position must be set to 1 for the goal to be achieved.
K represents the minimum total cost of the chosen operations, not the count.
Any valid solution with minimal cost is acceptable.
inline_prompts: There is an integer sequence x = (x_1, \ldots, x_N), which is initialized with x_1 = \cdots = x_N = 0. You will perform M operations on this integer sequence. In the i-th operation, you are given an integer pair (L_i, R_i) such that 1 \leq L_i \leq R_i \leq N, and you must perform exactly one of the following three operations: Setting it once is sufficient; additional sets have no effect on the goal. - Operation 0: Do nothing. This operation incurs a cost of 0. - Operation 1: For each integer j with 1 \leq j \leq N, if L_i \leq j \leq R_i holds, set x_j = 1. This operation incurs a cost of 1. - Operation 2: For each integer j with 1 \leq j \leq N, if L_i \leq j \leq R_i does not hold, set x_j = 1. This operation incurs a cost of 1. Your goal is to make x_1 = \cdots = x_N = 1 hold at the end. Determine whether this goal can be achieved. If it can be achieved, present one way to achieve it where the total cost of the operations is minimized. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N M L_1 R_1 \vdots L_M R_M Output If the goal is not achievable, print -1. If the goal is achievable, print one way to achieve it where the total cost of the operations, in the following format K \mathrm{op}_1 \cdots \mathrm{op}_M Constraints - 1 \leq N \leq 1000000 - 1 \leq M \leq 200000 - 1 \leq L_i \leq R_i \leq N - All input values are integers.
